div.head: Cn 1020 18
div.ab: ⁊ gyt we furðor maniað, þæt man Sunnandæges freols mid eallum mægene healde ⁊ weorðige fram Sæternesdæges none oð Monandæges lyhtinge, ⁊ nan man swa dyrstig ne sy, þæt he aðor oððe cypinge wyrce oððe ænig mot gesæce þam halgan dæge.

⁊ gyt we furðor maniað, þæt man Sunnandæges freols mid eallum mægene healde ⁊ weorðige fram Sæternesdæges none oð Monandæges lyhtinge, ⁊ nan man swa dyrstig ne sy, þæt he aðor oððe cypinge wyrce oððe ænig mot gesæce [on] þam halgan dæge.

And gyt we furðor maniað þæt man Sunnandæges freols mid eallum mægene healde and weorðige fram Sæternesdæges none oð Monandæges lyhtinge, and nan man swa dyrstig ne sy þæt he aðor oððe cypinge wyrce oððe ænig mot gesece on þam halgan dæge.

Und wir ermahnen ferner noch, dass man Sonntagsfeier mit aller Kraft halte und ehre von des Sonnabends Mittagszeit bis Montags Morgenroth; und niemand sei so frech, dass er entweder Kaufhandel treibe oder eine Gerichtsversammlung besuche an dem heiligen Tage.

And we further urge that the Sunday festival be kept and honoured with all [our] strength from Saturday noon until Monday dawn; and let no one be so presumptuous as either to trade or attend any court on that holy day.

And further still we admonish all men to keep and observe the Sunday festival with all their might from noon on Saturday till dawn on Monday, and no man shall be so preumptuous as either to trade or to attend any assembly on the holy day.

And moreover we admonish that the Sunday festival is to be observed and honoured with all one’s might from Saturday noon until dawn on Monday, and that no one is to be so presumptuous as either to carry on any trading or to attend any meeting on that holy day.

And we yet further emphasize that the Sunday holy day is to be kept and honored with all effort from midafternoon Saturday until dawn on Monday, and no one is to be so bold as to either transact business or attend any meeting on that holy day.
